pr_title: Store ZHA light brightness when fading off to turn on at the correct brightness
pr_body:
## Description:
Previously, if the light is turned off with a time transition, the brightness level stored in the light will be 1. The next time the light is turned on with no explicit brightness, it will be at 1.

This can be solved by storing the current brightness before turning off, and then using that when turning on.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #26374

  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**

pr_comments:
but the light it self still has the brightness 0/1%. I'm talking about wall switches like 45857GE. If we do transition to Off, then next time you turn on the light from the switch itself, it still would come on at 1%

Also, lights will send level reports every 15 min and it would send level of 1% which would also override the level. 

Perhaps for turning off the light with transition, we should set the transition time in `OffTransitionTime` attribute and just issue `Off` command. That would take care of properly  restore the level. Although i don't know how may times you can write to `OffTransitionTime`  as it is going to wear NVRAM off. My recommendation is to manually set `OffTransitiontime` attribute and then just issue Off command to the light.
And of course 45857GE does not support off transition time attribute :E  But OSRAM works fine with that setup.

Just refactored this to store the brightness on HA. 
Turning the light on from a zigbee switch that is directly binded to the light will still show the wrong behavior, unless the user manually sets the on_level on the light. But from HA everything should work as expected.

**Description of problem:**

**Additional information:**
It seems that the ZHA component updates the light brightness in HA during the transition period.
comments: Hey there @dmulcahey, @adminiuga, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`zha`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L321) for? Thanks!

@dmulcahey I think during the transition, especially the longer ones,, the light sends level attribute update which overwrites the current brightness.  Maybe we should ignore level attribute reports during the transition and while the light is off?
🤷‍♂ wonder what the best way to do that is...

I'm open to ideas how to handle this better. We could remove "Off Transition" then the light itself is going to retain the level to turn on. 
Alternatively, for `turn_on` service we could set brightness level to whatever HA thinks it is. But it probably going to be out of sync and then we'll start receiving complainants from other users.

@abmantis in Zigbee, the only way to do a "turn off transition" is to send `move_to_level` command with level 0. This effectively changes the light's "current" level to 1% so the light next time you turn on the light, it comes up with minimal brightness. 
You either have to specify the "brightness" in `turn_on` service call or don't use transitions for `turn_off` calls.

this https://github.com/Adminiuga/home-assistant/commit/5bc75a7f1261173e408202aee25710333b45002b only half solves the problem. At least it would restore the previous HA level as long as you `turn_on` service with a `transition` attribute. If you however turn on the light from the switch, then it still comes up at minimal level, cause that the level it was moved to.

Yes, it is inconsistent with other integrations but it  is the only way you can do a transition to off in zigbee. The only other workaround I can think of, is always to turn on the light to Max brightness or last saved brightness prior the transition if the light reports 1% Brightness or less, obviously this is far from ideal and the problem still remains bwith the wall switches as those still will turn on at minimal brightness if controlled from the switch locally

review_comments: Should we add `self.brihtness < 15` here as well? I just want if the light was operated from the switch and not from HA and it reported the brightness value, then it should be used instead. This is to ensure the off brightness is used only if it was an off transition.
In that case, isn't it better to clear the off_brightness when the lamp reports that it was turned on?
Hrm, we could do it in "set_level" if the normalized value > 15 then clear `off_brighness`
I agree we should do it there. But I don't think we should check if > 15. If the light goes on, it is on and off_brightness should be cleared.
Actually, I think off_brightness should be cleared in async_set_state, if state is True.

Good point. We should do both. If the light was actioned externally and we get on_off attribute update -> off_brightness is cleared. If HA successfully called all of the `light.turn_on` service -> clear off_brightness.

The problem with clearing off_brightness only on `set_state()` some lights (HUE) do not report states, so it never would be cleared.
and I agree, if we clear `off_brightness` in `set_state()` then no need for `self.brightness > 15`
